walkthroughs.body_html:
d-t: gradient = velocity.

v-t: gradient = acceleration; area = distance.

Add vectors head to tail.

Resultant zero -> equilibrium or constant velocity.

Weight initially > drag -> accelerates down.

Drag rises with speed until weight = drag: terminal velocity.

mcqs.q: If an object is moving at constant velocity in a straight line, what is the net force on it?
options: There must be a forward force on the object to keep it moving.
Negative acceleration means the car is moving backwards.
Zero — by Newton's first law, constant velocity requires zero net force.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.

mcqs.q: If a car has negative acceleration, what does that necessarily mean?
options: Its acceleration is in the negative direction (often opposite to the chosen positive direction); it may be slowing down or speeding up in reverse.
Negative acceleration always means the car is slowing down.
Negative acceleration means the car is moving backwards.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.

mcqs.q: If air resistance is ignored, which falls faster: a heavy ball or a light ball dropped from the same height?
options: The lighter ball falls faster because it has less inertia.
Heavier objects fall faster than lighter objects because gravity pulls more on them.
Both fall at the same rate because gravitational acceleration is independent of mass.
Negative acceleration means the car is moving backwards.
